text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- King Hussein and Queen Noor depart to the U.S. where the king will meet U.S. President Clinton and senior officials on bilateral ties and developments in the Middle East peace process.
- Jordan condemns the Tel Aviv cafe suicide blast and calls for restraint; says peace is the only option for all parties.
- Prime Minister Abdul-Salam al-Majali says Jordan will use its relations with Israel to serve the Palestinians.
- Details of a plan to improve salaries of judges and buttress the independence of the judiciary.
- Majali meets PLO's Farouk Kaddoumi and stresses "principled stance in support of the Palestinian people's right to nationhood and legitimate rights."
- New government to push ahead with economic reforms; with two main teams handling a broad range of issues from administrative reform to boosting competitiveness of local industry.
- King heads for U.S. after instructing security forces to be alert against infiltrators.
